storyboard.claim: Rule number one: don't cry, no matter what.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Three Rules card — a numbered list — shown large. Will stands blank-faced beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open — the first rule stated plainly.
storyboard.addedInformation: The theRules icon is the literal numbered list from the poem; blind viewer reads 'a list of rules'.

storyboard.claim: Rule number two: don't snitch, no matter what.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Rules card again — the second line highlighted. Will unmoved.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list from beat 0.
storyboard.addedInformation: Repeating the theRules icon across consecutive beats reinforces the list structure; callout changes each time.

storyboard.claim: Rule three: if someone kills a person you love, find and kill them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Rules card — third line. The word 'revenge' hangs. Will's face stays blank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the three-rule list from beats 0–1.
storyboard.addedInformation: All three rules now on screen; blank expression signals Will is already inside them, not reacting.

storyboard.claim: These rules are terrifying because they are not suggestions; they are laws.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will thinking, face worried — the weight of the rules pressing down.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts react to the rules they just laid out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Will's worried + think reads as someone weighing something heavy, which is exactly right.

storyboard.claim: These are laws written by the dead, not casual street wisdom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The law icon — a gavel or scroll — alongside Will's afraid face. The authorship of the rules is the dead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Upgrades beat 3: from 'terrifying' to 'authored by ghosts'.
storyboard.addedInformation: law icon reads as law, courts, legal authority — exact meaning here: these ARE law in Will's world.

storyboard.claim: The hosts came in expecting a suspenseful thriller.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will standing neutral — the 'before' state, before the real architecture was visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot to meta-commentary on the book's reception.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no icon cleanly captures 'expectation of a thriller'; staging Will neutral signals this is setup, not payoff.

storyboard.claim: The surface read: will this 15-year-old pull the trigger or not?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will holding the gun — literally the premise the hosts thought they were in for.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concretizes beat 5's 'thriller' framing with the gun in hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: theGun icon + hold action makes the question literal and physical.

storyboard.claim: Reading it, they realized they had the entirely wrong blueprint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will's face: surprised — the realization. The callout strikes through the wrong frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reversal of beats 5–6: the thriller expectation is dismissed.
storyboard.addedInformation: strike style signals the hosts are rejecting their own prior framing.

storyboard.claim: The suspense is not about the gun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will with the theGun icon visible but struck through by the callout — the gun is present but not the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the framing established in beat 6.
storyboard.addedInformation: strike callout on the theGun icon is the clearest possible negation; blank face = the gun is hollow.

storyboard.claim: The book is a relentless 60-second cross-examination of an inherited code.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The theRules icon — the code on trial. Will thinking, worried, as if under examination.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the book actually is, after beats 7–8 cleared the wrong frames.
storyboard.addedInformation: theRules icon is exactly what is being cross-examined; worried + think is the pressure of that examination.

storyboard.claim: The code is inherited from the ghosts of the neighborhood's past.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Inheritance icon — a will, an estate — the rules passed down like property. Will afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens beat 9: the code is not invented, it is received.
storyboard.addedInformation: inheritance reads as 'a will, an heir' — exactly the transmission of the rules from the dead.

storyboard.claim: The elevator is a courtroom; a ghost boards on every floor as a character witness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floorCounter icon — elevator doors with descending numbers. Will afraid, Shawn a ghost beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First concrete setting detail: the elevator structure of the novel.
storyboard.addedInformation: floorCounter is this book's clock — the countdown of the trial. Shawn as ghost makes 'character witnesses' literal.

storyboard.claim: The verse form itself — words on the page — is the ticking clock of the trial.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Clock icon — time running, deadline. Will afraid: every second the elevator descends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the formal layer: the poem's shape IS the clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: clock reads as time, deadline — correct here. The elevator is both spatial and temporal.

storyboard.claim: The prosecution tears apart Will's reality piece by piece, floor by floor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: floorCounter counting down; Will slumped — his foundation crumbling under him.
storyboard.onScreenText: Piece by piece, floor by floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The trial metaphor becomes a demolition: each floor strips a belief.
storyboard.addedInformation: slump reads as deflation, defeat — his world being dismantled.

storyboard.claim: Ground zero: Will is 15 years old.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will, full figure in room — just a child, small and slight in his hoodie. Blank face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Hosts shift to grounding the reader in the story's starting point.
storyboard.addedInformation: No icon needed — his physical smallness and youth must be the image.

storyboard.claim: Will's older brother Shawn was shot dead in the street the day before.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shawn collapsed on the street. Will beside him, face sad. Grave icon for the death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the inciting event: Shawn's death.
storyboard.addedInformation: collapsed reads as 'fallen / dead' — exactly right. grave icon confirms the death is recent and real.

storyboard.claim: Will has Shawn's gun tucked in his waistband — cold against his skin.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will holding the gun, face afraid. The physical weight and cold are the sensation named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the death in beat 15 to what Will carries because of it.
storyboard.addedInformation: theGun icon makes the inheritance literal: the gun passed from the dead to the living.

storyboard.claim: Will steps into the elevator on the eighth floor and presses the lobby button.
storyboard.concreteVisual: floorCounter showing '8' — the starting point. Will walking in, face blank, the descent beginning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The physical action that starts the novel proper.
storyboard.addedInformation: floorCounter is the book's own icon for this exact moment.

storyboard.claim: Going down means descending into an underworld where the rules demand blood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will falling — the descent is literal and metaphorical. Grave icon: the underworld of the dead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The elevator button pressed in beat 17 — now the meaning of the descent named.
storyboard.addedInformation: falling reads as 'falling, plunging' — the descent into the underworld. afraid face carries the dread.

storyboard.claim: The prefrontal cortex — the planning and consequences brain — is not fully developed at 15.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will thinking, worried. No icon for a brain region; the face and posture carry the psychological claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Before the elevator: the hosts explain Will's mental state.
storyboard.addedInformation: worried + think reads as someone wrestling with something; the callout supplies the science.

storyboard.claim: The undeveloped brain operates in extreme black and white — and then receives the worst trauma imaginable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank and still — the absolutism of an unfinished mind absorbing catastrophe.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the trauma layer: the developmental limit plus grief.
storyboard.addedInformation: blank reads as apathy, numbness — the brain shut down under extreme binary thinking.

storyboard.claim: Before Will even leaves his apartment, Reynolds gives a visceral metaphor for what he is feeling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will lying in his bedroom — the apartment is still home, the metaphor has not been revealed yet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts announce the tooth metaphor is coming; the bedroom grounds it in place.
storyboard.addedInformation: lying reads as 'lying in bed' — correct, he is in his bedroom before stepping out.

storyboard.claim: The tooth thing: his grief feels like a raw nerve — electric pain, no relief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped, afraid, the crack icon behind him — grief splitting open like a raw nerve.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same bedroom scene — the hosts identify the specific metaphor by name.
storyboard.addedInformation: lying in bedroom is correct action/set combo per the rules.

callout.text: Grip a back tooth and rip.

storyboard.claim: Reynolds describes grief as a stranger strapping you down, gripping a back tooth with pliers and ripping it out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will struggling — the physical metaphor of being held down and having something torn from you.
storyboard.onScreenText: Grip a back tooth and rip.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tooth metaphor described now in visceral detail.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: struggling alone reads as 'recoiling/startled' per the rules note, but the callout anchors the extraction violence. Second cast member not added as the stranger is unnamed and figurative.

storyboard.claim: The physical trauma of the image is deliberate: Reynolds is not saying he is sad but that something has been violently extracted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped — past the violence, now the aftermath. Face: grief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts interpret the metaphor: this is not ordinary sadness.
storyboard.addedInformation: slump reads as deflation, defeat — aftermath of the extraction.

storyboard.claim: The metaphor: knocking in your head, pressure in your ears, blood pooling in your mouth — but the hosts are blown away by what comes next.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped, face sad — the physical cascade of grief sensations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the physical detail of the tooth metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout is the concrete sensory phrase from the narration; staging unchanged — still in the aftermath.

storyboard.claim: The worst part: your tongue keeps slipping into the empty space where the tooth was but isn't anymore.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will thinking — the obsessive probing of absence. Face: sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The turn in the metaphor — from extraction to obsession with the void.
storyboard.addedInformation: think reads as probing, dwelling — the obsessive mental return to the absence.

storyboard.claim: This changes the definition of grief: not a quiet sadness but a physical amputation — violent removal of a part of your anatomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped, Shawn the ghost beside him — the brother who was amputated. Abstract set: the idea space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts name the new definition of grief unlocked by the metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shawn appears here to make 'your brother is gone' literal — the amputated part stands beside Will.

storyboard.claim: It is not a tear rolling down a cheek at a photograph — it is a violent removal. Your brother is gone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will holding a photo — the image the narration contrasts with. Face: grief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Holds the 'photograph' image from the narration while naming what is truly lost.
storyboard.addedInformation: photo icon + hold makes the contrast literal: this is NOT the gentle grief of looking at a photo.

storyboard.claim: Into this gaping, bleeding wound, the rules are poured.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The theRules icon — the list of three. Will afraid and still: the rules fill the absence of his brother.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The grief (beats 22–28) meets the rules — the rules enter through the wound.
storyboard.addedInformation: theRules appearing after the grief section makes the causal link concrete: wound → rules fill it.

callout.text: Meant for the broken to follow.

storyboard.claim: Will states it as undisputed law: the rules were not meant to be broken — they were meant for the broken to follow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: theRules icon. Will blank — he is already submitted, not deliberating.
storyboard.onScreenText: Meant for the broken to follow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Echoes beats 0–2 but now with full grief context: we know WHY the broken follow them.
storyboard.addedInformation: blank reads as apathy, numbness — submission to the law, not resistance.

storyboard.claim: It is absolute dogma: you don't debate, you submit — and everyone falls in line immediately.
storyboard.concreteVisual: theRules on street — the rules enacted in public space. Will blank: already in line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from individual grief to collective submission in the street.
storyboard.addedInformation: Moving to street set anticipates the shooting scene in beats 32–35.

storyboard.claim: Right after the shooting: sirens, a young cop, a newbie who actually expects someone to answer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will on the street, blank — the neighborhood after the shooting. The cop's question hangs unanswered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The scene after Shawn's shooting — the rules in action.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the cop is not a named cast member; Will holds the scene as the community's representative.

storyboard.claim: The cop asks the crowd if anyone saw anything. Nobody says a word.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank on the street — the silence of the crowd embodied in one person.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cop's question from beat 32, now quoted exactly.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quoted question appears on screen; the blank face is the silence as the answer.

storyboard.claim: Marcus Andrews, the neighborhood know-it-all, instinctively says 'I ain't seen nothing' — even the man who knows everything knows better than to know anything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank on the street — Marcus is unnamed cast so Will carries the collective voice. The callout is the quote.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Specific person now named responding to the question in beat 33.
storyboard.addedInformation: The irony is in the callout text; the blank face = compliant silence.

storyboard.claim: Rule number two enforced: everyone obeys because the environment demands it. The threat is absolute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: theRules on the street — the rule applied in real time. Will blank: submission in action.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names and summarizes the silence of beats 33–34 as Rule 2.
storyboard.addedInformation: theRules icon brings the abstract rule back to the concrete street scene.

storyboard.claim: Gunshots make everybody deaf and blind — this is mass psychological conditioning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon — bound, controlled. The neighborhood is collectively held by an invisible force. Will blank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Interprets the silence as conditioning, not cowardice.
storyboard.addedInformation: chains reads as 'bound, controlled' — correct for psychological conditioning; NOT for numbness (per rules).

storyboard.claim: One host's first instinct: these brutal rules are actually a harsh but necessary survival mechanism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shield icon — protection. Will thinking, worried: the defense argument being considered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts move from observing the rules to evaluating them — first the defense.
storyboard.addedInformation: shield reads as protection — exactly the argument being made: the rules protect the community.

storyboard.claim: In a system where cops don't protect and courts don't deliver justice, the rules maintain a terrifying order.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Law icon — a gavel/scroll representing the official justice that fails this community. Will thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Grounds the 'survival mechanism' argument in systemic failure.
storyboard.addedInformation: law icon represents the absent official law — its presence here is ironic: the formal system doesn't show up.

storyboard.claim: The two hosts split: one sees the rules as the neighborhood's immune system; the other vehemently disagrees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter diagram with two buckets: 'Immune system' vs 'Suicide pact' (from context beat 41). Will thinking between them.
storyboard.onScreenText: Immune system vs. suicide pact — two readings of the same rules.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The debate crystallizes: beat 37's defense vs the coming rebuttal (context beat 40–41).
storyboard.addedInformation: The sorter diagram replaces icon + callout on this structural pivot beat where two readings are formally compared.
